data.title: A trail in the midnight log
story: The SOC team found odd lines in the server log: an "auto backup" job owned by the account helper-kode ran at midnight and left a random-looking note.
The note is Base64 (a way of writing data as letters and digits). Inside it is a Caesar cipher shifted by 3. Undo both to find the flag.

artifacts.label: Server log excerpt
artifacts.content:

artifacts.label: Python hint: reading Base64
artifacts.content:
import binascii
text = binascii.a2b_base64(b"SGVsbG8=").decode()
print(text)   # Hello

data.scratch:
import binascii
note = b"SU9ESntOSE9ERVhfV1VETE99"
text = binascii.a2b_base64(note).decode()
print(text)
data.solution:
import binascii
note = b"SU9ESntOSE9ERVhfV1VETE99"
text = binascii.a2b_base64(note).decode()
print(text)
result = ""
for ch in text:
    if "A" <= ch <= "Z":
        result = result + chr((ord(ch) - ord("A") - 3) % 26 + ord("A"))
    else:
        result = result + ch
print(result)

explanation: Base64 is not protection, only a way to rewrite data, so a2b_base64() opens it straight away; the result is then shifted back 3 letters. Disguised data like this in a log is a warning sign to report to the SOC.
hints: Run the console first. The Base64 result looks like a Caesar cipher, right?
Shift every letter A to Z back by 3 with ord() and chr(), like the shift 1 exercise.
